attack_probe_schedule.name: unauthenticated_endpoint_scan
attack_probe_schedule.description: Scan for endpoints accessible without authentication
attack_probe_schedule.note: Cycle-16 batch-34 RE-SCAN over spacetimedb/nginx/vaultwarden/postgresql/ollama (2026-07-26, CVE scan + unauthenticated_endpoint_scan; 2-day re-check of the batch-33 cohort). 1 NEW item (REM-136, vaultwarden MEDIUM) + 1 closed (REM-135, spacetimedb). The probe's finding of record this batch: vaultwarden's unauth surface is WIDER than previously recorded. Prior batches leaned on the 127.0.0.1:8062 host bind to call the unauth legs 'LAN/insider-scoped', but that bind only constrains the DIRECT container port — traefik_auth_modes.vaultwarden='oidc' attaches NO forward-auth middleware to the auto-published Host(`pass.<tld>`) router, so anonymous HTTPS transits the edge into the app over iiab_net/shared_net. That makes the new icon-endpoint SSRF pair (GHSA-hw4g-2v3f-74x5, GHSA-vh5m-fc9v-m84g) and the unauth WebSocket flooding DDoS (GHSA-96f7-78q5-j345, against a hub that compose.yml.j2:23 enables unconditionally) anonymously reachable by anyone who can resolve the tenant TLD. Rated MEDIUM, not HIGH: SSRF is blind-ish and the WS leg is availability-only, SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false, and no internet exposure unless the TLD is publicly routed. GENERAL LESSON for future native_oidc services: 'oidc' in traefik_auth_modes means the EDGE IS OPEN and the app's own login is the only gate — pre-auth endpoints (icons, websockets, health, well-known) of every native_oidc service are anonymously reachable and must be scored as such. The other four components re-confirmed with no anonymously-reachable exposure: spacetimedb (loopback host-map + install flag off), nginx (install_nginx=false default; Traefik is the edge), postgresql (loopback, no HTTP, no router), ollama (OLLAMA_HOST=127.0.0.1 loopback bind is the sole control for the still-unpatched CVE-2026-5757).

It did NOT verify image signatures or provenance attestations, did not diff layer contents against upstream build recipes, and did not audit the language-level dependency manifests inside any image. Absence of a finding on those axes is absence of a test, not evidence of cleanliness.

Probe produced ONE finding of its own class (REM-209, onlyoffice) plus one CVE-leg finding (REM-208, erpnext). The probe-class result: of five components, exactly one discloses its version to an anonymous caller at the edge, and it does so in the RESPONSE BODY while its Server header reads a bare 'nginx' -- /index.html and /web-apps/apps/api/documents/api.js both serve 'Version: 9.3.1'. A header-only probe of this class would have reported all five CLEAN and been wrong about one; read the body. The four measured-clean comparators are recorded in their component notes so the negative result is not re-derived: homeassistant blanks Server: to an empty string on every path, firefly returns bare 'nginx' and 302s anonymous callers to Authentik, ntfy emits no Server header and no version, erpnext is not running and was honestly marked NOT ASSESSABLE. Both sources must be queried. (2) REM-167's Authentik mitigation for ntfy is falsified -- forward-auth was removed 2026-08-08 so phones could subscribe -- though its severity survives, since publish now requires a credential in ntfy's own user DB. Also established: four of the five components are LIVE despite every prior batch citing install_X=false, because config.yml overrides the default for ntfy, homeassistant, firefly and onlyoffice; only erpnext is genuinely absent.

Two of five components moved clean->affected in the 13 days since batch-46, and NEITHER move was visible to OSV -- portainer's nine OSV hits were all Go-range false positives while the real CRITICAL sat only on the vendor GHSA endpoint. Clean and honestly so: openwebui 0.11.0 sits at or above all 30 published fix lines, postgresql 16.14 IS the fix line for the newest PG cohort (16.15 exists but carries no security content -- a bare latest-vs-pin check would misfire), bluesky_pds has zero advisories across the pds repo, the atproto repo and four @atproto npm packages.

Second run of this probe (first was cycle-30 over bone/wing/pulse/miniflux/nodered -> REM-203). It produced one estate-wide finding and two component-level ones, and the estate-wide one is the finding of record: the estate declares mem_limit on 53 of 53 compose templates and 60 of 60 running containers, and declares pids_limit or ulimits on ZERO of either -- so it controls the two axes that are easy to reason about and neither of the two a fork bomb or fd exhaustion uses, against a Docker VM whose kernel.pid_max (99999) and fs.file-max (2,379,288) are shared by all 60 containers (REM-219). The same row records that the memory control it DOES have is not an aggregate one: 54.75 GiB of mem_limit committed against 22.7 GiB of VM, 241 per cent, or 482 with Docker's implicit 2x memswap. Component-level: FreeScout accepts a 2G upload into a 512m container with max_execution_time 0, where the memory leg is mitigated by nginx/PHP spooling to disk but the disk and worker-occupancy legs are not (REM-220); and not one of 41 live Traefik routers carries a rateLimit, inFlightReq or buffering middleware, which Outline currently survives only because outlinewiki ships its limiter on by default -- a control in the dependency rather than the deployment (REM-221). COVERAGE CEILING, stated rather than implied. TWO of the five components were NOT MEASURED: qgis_server and superset both resolve install=false and neither is in docker ps, so they got template review only -- a regression in coverage from batch-48/49, which measured both running. Their latent template hazards are named in their component notes and deliberately NOT filed as rows, because a service with no deployment has no exposure. For the three live services, NO EXHAUSTION WAS EXECUTED -- no fork storm, no memory balloon, no 2G upload, no connection flood was driven against the operator's live estate. Every figure is read from the Docker daemon's own accounting, the containers' own config files, and the rendered Traefik config. Also untested on every component: disk-quota exhaustion of the host bind mounts (headroom measured at 53 GiB of 460, consumption not attempted), PostgreSQL and Redis connection-pool exhaustion from a saturating client, and any exhaustion path through the Authentik outpost that gates three of these five routers.
